sources.claim: A Maven project declares coordinates, conventional source/test layout, dependencies, plugins, and lifecycle phases so a clean environment can reproduce test and package outputs.

canonicalExplanation.summary: **Maven** builds Java projects from one file, **`pom.xml`**. It declares the project's **coordinates** (groupId, artifactId, version), its **dependencies** with exact versions, and **plugins** that do the work. Maven expects a **conventional layout**: code in `src/main/java`, tests in `src/test/java`. You run **lifecycle phases**, and each phase runs all the ones before it: `mvn test` compiles and tests, `mvn package` also builds the jar, and `mvn verify` adds integration checks. A build is only **reproducible** if everything it needs is in the committed pom: no hand-copied jars, no IDE-only settings, no "latest" versions, and tests that don't depend on your machine.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A learner's project builds in their IDE, but a teammate's `mvn package` fails: a library jar was added by hand to the IDE, and one test reads a file from the learner's Desktop. A month later the same pom produces a different jar because a plugin version wasn't pinned. mvn verify compiles main and test sources, runs deterministic tests, and produces a versioned artifact from the committed pom.xml. In this lesson you'll build, test and package a multi-package application with Maven.


sections.heading: The model: pom, layout, lifecycle
sections.body:
```xml
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0">
  <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>
  <groupId>com.shop</groupId>          <!-- coordinates. -->
  <artifactId>shop-cli</artifactId>
  <version>1.0.0</version>

  <properties>
    <maven.compiler.release>21</maven.compiler.release>
    <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>
  </properties>

  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
      <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
      <version>5.10.2</version>          <!-- exact version. -->
      <scope>test</scope>                <!-- only for tests. -->
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>
</project>
```

```text
shop-cli/
  pom.xml
  src/main/java/com/shop/billing/Payments.java
  src/main/java/com/shop/app/Main.java
  src/test/java/com/shop/billing/PaymentsTest.java

mvn clean verify   ->  validate, compile, test, package, verify
                   ->  target/shop-cli-1.0.0.jar
```

```reveal
{"prompt": "What does the test scope mean?", "answer": "The dependency is available when compiling and running tests, but it isn't part of the main code or packaged as a runtime dependency."}
```

examples.title: mvn verify from a clean checkout
examples.situation: mvn verify compiles main and test sources, runs deterministic tests, and produces a versioned artifact from the committed pom.xml.
walkthrough: **mvn verify compiles main and test sources:** compile and test-compile run first.
**Runs deterministic tests:** any failing test stops the build.
**Produces a versioned artifact from the committed pom.xml:** target/shop-cli-1.0.0.jar, and we check a fresh clone builds the same.
examples.result: Anyone can reproduce the build and its tests with one command.

examples.title: Works on my machine
examples.situation: A teammate's build fails because a jar was added through the IDE and a test reads a file from the author's Desktop.
walkthrough: Declare the library as a dependency in pom.xml.
Move the test file into src/test/resources and load it from the classpath.
Run mvn clean verify in a fresh clone to prove it.
examples.result: The build passes on every machine and in CI.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: If mvn package succeeds once, the pom fully captures the build and the same artifact is guaranteed everywhere.
misconceptions.correction: One success can depend on local jars, caches, unpinned versions or machine-specific files. Pin versions and verify from a clean checkout.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "Works on my machine", what wasn't captured by the pom?

analogy.example: A pom.xml is like **a precise recipe card** for a bakery chain. It lists exact ingredients and brands (dependencies with versions) and the standard steps in order (lifecycle phases). If a baker quietly adds a secret spice from their own cupboard (a hand-added jar), the other branches can't bake the same cake.
limitations: Each step includes the earlier ones: you can't ice before baking.
CI is a new branch baking from the card alone.

steps.explanation: Removing old outputs means nothing stale affects the build.
mvn verify compiles main and test sources and runs deterministic tests.
It produces a versioned artifact from the committed pom.xml.

trace.textAlternative: Tracing the Maven lifecycle. Step 1, Clean: target/ is deleted. Removing old outputs means nothing stale affects the build. Step 2, Verify: phases is compile, test, package, verify; tests is all pass. mvn verify compiles main and test sources and runs deterministic tests. Step 3, Artifact: jar is shop-cli-1.0.0.jar. It produces a versioned artifact from the committed pom.xml.

remediation.explanation: After any build change, run **mvn clean verify in a fresh clone**. If it fails, something the build needs is outside the pom.
